R678.note: th:text blanket-escapes everything instead of implementing the contract's allowlist sanitization, so intentionally-supported rich-text tags no longer render at all (regressed to plain text, not preserved) - stated openly in the explanation but not the required shape.

R679.note: Wraps exportUsersHandler with the existing requireAdmin middleware, mirroring the ban/unban pattern exactly; no other observable change.

R680.note: Adds bcrypt.compare against the stored hash before authenticating, standard passport-local fix; failure path returns done(null, false, ...) as passport expects.

R681.note: Converts the state-changing GET to POST with [ValidateAntiForgeryToken], the standard ASP.NET Core fix for this exact finding shape; write-up openly notes the confirmation view must post the token.

R682.note: Drops cmd.exe/shell string entirely for a direct ping.exe argument-array invocation; closes the injection vector without adding any new restriction on legitimate input.

R683.note: Numbered placeholders with ids passed as the parameter array; returns every matching order for any size array, matching the stated contract.

R684.note: Re-reads tasks[activeIndex] by index after the invalidating push_back instead of reusing the stale reference; earlier valid uses of current are left untouched.

R685.note: Sets XmlResolver = null before LoadXml, the standard XmlDocument XXE fix; no other behavior change for documents without external entities.

R686.note: Switches to JNDI parameterized filter substitution ({0}/{1} with filterArgs), letting DirContext.search perform RFC-compliant escaping; argument order/semantics match the original intent.

R687.note: Replaces fmt.Sprintf string building with a placeholder plus separate QueryRow argument, the standard database/sql parameterization pattern.

R688.note: Captures bytesSent() into a local before the unique_ptr reset instead of reading through the dangling raw pointer afterward; preserves the documented 'bytes from the original send' return value.

R689.note: Canonicalization plus startsWith containment check is the correct core fix, but the added blanket param.contains("..") pre-check rejects any filename containing a literal '..' substring even when it wouldn't escape the directory (e.g. 'notes..txt'), a restriction the original accepted and the write-up doesn't flag as a tradeoff.

R690.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes'=>false]) blocks PHP object-injection gadget chains but the contract requires unsigned attacker cookies to no longer reach unserialize() at all (implying a signature check); attacker-controlled payloads still transit unserialize(), just without object construction. Empty-cart and legitimate items/coupon shape are both preserved, so no additional harm is introduced.
